Definition: a strengthened form of a primary τέκω (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively:--bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.
BiblicalUsage: This is the ordinary word for bringing forth, whether a child or a crop. Paul quotes Isaiah's barren woman who bears children in Galatians 4:27, and Hebrews says the earth that drinks in the rain brings forth herbs and receives blessing from God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is simple and steady: life that bears fruit is life that has first received, whether rain from heaven or promise from God.
